description: The aim of this book is to present the statistical and mathematical principles of smoothing with a focus on applicable techniques. The necessary mathematical treatment is easily understandable and a wide variety of interactive smoothing examples are given.

title: Applied Nonparametric Regression
author: Wolfgang K. Hardle
description: This book focuses on the applications and practical problems of two central aspects of curve smoothing: the choice of smoothing parameters and the construction of confidence bounds.

title: Multivariate Statistical Analysis in the Real and Complex Domains
author: Unknown
description: This book explores topics in multivariate statistical analysis, relevant in the real and complex domains. It utilizes simplified and unified notations to render the complex subject matter both accessible and enjoyable, drawing from clear exposition.

title: Applied Multivariate Statistical Analysis
author: Wolfgang K. Hardle
description: This book gives a broad and modern introduction to statistics for multivariate data. A bunch of interesting examples is used to illustrate the techniques.

title: Theory and Applications of Monte Carlo Simulations
author: Wai Kin Chan
description: The purpose of this book is to introduce researchers and practitioners to recent advances and applications of Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS). Random sampling is the key of the MCS technique.

title: Applications of Monte Carlo Method in Science and Engineering
author: Unknown
description: This book exposes the broad range of applications of Monte Carlo simulation in the fields of Quantum Physics, Statistical Physics, Reliability, Medical Physics, Polycrystalline Materials, Ising Model, Chemistry, Agriculture, Food Processing, X-ray Imaging, ...

title: Statistical Tools for Finance and Insurance
author: Pavel Cizek, et al
description: This book presents ready-to-use solutions, theoretical developments and method construction for many practical problems in quantitative finance and insurance.

title: Statistics: Methods and Applications
author: Thomas Hill, et al
description: This book offers a comprehensive, almost encyclopedic presentation of statistical methods and analytic approaches used in science, industry, business, and data mining, written from the perspective of the real-life practitioner ('consumer') of these methods.

title: Introductory Statistics
author: T. H. Wonnacott, et al
description: This book is an introduction to statistics for students of economics or business, suitable for a one or two-semester course, yet uses the simplest mathematics consistent with a sound presentation.

title: Natural Image Statistics in Digital Image Forensics
author: Siwei Lyu
description: This book provides the first general framework, based on universal statistical properties of natural images, of detecting tampering and authenticating digital images that has been successfully applied to three problems in digital image forensics.

title: Introduction to Statistical Signal Processing
author: Robert M. Gray, et al
description: This book describes the essential tools and techniques of statistical signal processing, with specific applications to the analysis of random signals and systems for communicating, estimating, detecting, modulating, etc.

title: Window Functions and Their Applications in Signal Processing
author: Unknown
description: This book presents an exhaustive and detailed account of Window Functions and their applications in signal processing, focusing on the areas of digital spectral analysis, design of FIR filters, pulse compression radar, and speech signal processing.

title: A Practical Guide to Geostatistical Mapping
author: Tomislav Hengl
description: A practical guide to geostatistical mapping using R+gstat/geoR, SAGA GIS and Google Earth combo of software packages.

title: Using R for Introductory Statistics
author: John Verzani
description: This book lays the foundation for further study and development in statistics using R - an ideal text for integrating the study of statistics with a powerful computational tool.

title: Natural Image Statistics: A Probabilistic Approach
author: A. Hyvarinen
description: This book is both an introductory textbook and a research monograph on modelling the statistical structure of natural images. The statistical structure is described using a number of statistical models whose parameters are estimated from image samples.

title: Introduction to Calculus
author: J. H. Heinbockel
description: This textbook is an introductory calculus presentation intended for future scientists and engineers. Be sure that you have had the appropriate background material of algebra and trigonometry.

title: Understanding Basic Calculus
author: S. K. Chung
description: This textbook is an introductory calculus presentation intended for future scientists and engineers. Be sure that you have had the appropriate background material of algebra and trigonometry.

title: Fractional Calculus: Theory and Applications
author: Jorge E Macías Díaz
description: Fractional Calculus has led to tremendous progress in various areas of science and mathematics. New definitions of fractional derivatives and integrals have been uncovered, extending their classical definitions in various ways.

title: The Fractional Calculus: Theory and Applications
author: Unknown
description: Not only does it explain the theory (Fractional Calculus) underlying the properties of the generalized operator, but it also illustrates the wide variety of fields to which these ideas may be applied.

title: Calculus Made Easy
author: Silvanus P. Thompson
description: This book is a popular math book to help modern readers of all levels understand the subject on calculus through simple way and explanation. It's not just theory-based but contains exercises and answers so you can practice the understanding for each chapter.

title: Exercises and Problems in Calculus
author: John M. Erdman
description: Ideal for self-instruction as well as for classroom use, this text helps students improve their understanding and problem-solving skills in analysis, analytic geometry, and higher algebra.

title: Teaching and Learning of Calculus
author: David Bressoud, et al.
description: Focuses on the main trends in the field of calculus education. Despite their variety, the findings reveal a cornerstone issue that is strongly linked to the formalism of calculus concepts and to the difficulties it generates in the learning and teaching process.

title: Topics in Complex Analysis
author: Dan Romik
description: This graduate-level mathematics textbook provides an in-depth and readable exposition of selected topics in complex analysis. The focus is on beautiful applications of complex analysis to geometry and number theory.

title: Complex Variables with Applications
author: Jeremy Orloff
description: Complex variables offer very efficient methods for attacking many difficult problems, and it is the aim of this book to offer a thorough review of these methods and their applications.

title: Calculus
author: Gilbert Strang
description: This highly regarded calculus textbook is ideal as for self-study. Examples of apps of calculus to physics, engineering and economics are included, as well as many practice questions and illustrative diagrams to assist the reader's grasp of the material.

title: Yet Another Calculus Text: A Short Introduction with Infinitesimals
author: Unknown
description: An introduction to calculus based on the hyperreal number system so it uses infinitesimal and infinite numbers freely. It aims primarily at readers who already have some familiarity with calculus.

title: Measure, Integration and Real Analysis
author: Sheldon Axler
description: This textbook welcomes students into the fundamental theory of measure, integration, and real analysis. Focusing on an accessible approach, it lays the foundations for further study by promoting a deep understanding of key results.

title: Elementary Calculus
author: Michael Corral
description: This textbook covers calculus of a single variable, is designed for students who have completed courses in high-school algebra, geometry, and trigonometry. Though designed for college students, it could also be used in high schools.

title: Precalculus: An Investigation of Functions
author: David Lippman, et al
description: Comprehensive and evenly paced, this book provides complete coverage of the function concept, and integrates a significant amount of graphing calculator material to help students develop insight into mathematical ideas.

title: An Introduction to Measure Theory
author: Terrence Tao
description: This is a graduate text introducing the fundamentals of measure theory and integration theory, which is the foundation of modern real analysis, intended to cover a quarter or semester's worth of material for a first graduate course in real analysis.

title: Elementary Real Analysis
author: Brian S. Thomson, et al
description: This book is written in a rigorous, yet reader friendly style with motivational and historical material that emphasizes the 'big picture' and makes proofs seem natural rather than mysterious.

title: Real Variables with Basic Metric Space Topology
author: Robert B. Ash
description: Designed for a first course in real variables, this text presents the fundamentals for more advanced mathematical work, particularly in the areas of complex variables, measure theory, differential equations, functional analysis, and probability.

title: Hilbert Spaces And Operators On Hilbert Spaces
author: Leif Mejlbro
description: The book concisely presents the fundamental aspects of the theory of operators on Hilbert Spaces. The topics covered include functional calculus and spectral theorems, compact operators, trace class and Hilbert-Schmidt operators, etc.

title: How We Got from There to Here: A Story of Real Analysis
author: Unknown
description: This book is an introductory real analysis textbook, presented through the lens of history. The definitions and techniques are motivated by the actual difficulties encountered by the intuitive approach and are presented in their historical context.

title: Variational Analysis
author: R. Tyrrell Rockafellar, et al
description: This book develops a unified framework and, in finite dimension, provides a detailed exposition of variational geometry and subdifferential calculus in their current forms beyond classical and convex analysis.

title: The Art of Polynomial Interpolation
author: Stuart Murphy
description: Exploring the techniques of interpolating data allows us to view the development and birth of a polynomial. This book is focused on laying a foundation for understanding and applying several common forms of Polynomial Interpolation.

title: The Functional Analysis of Quantum Information Theory
author: Unknown
description: This book provides readers with a concise introduction to current studies on operator-algebras and their generalizations, operator spaces and operator systems, with a special focus on their application in Quantum Information Science.

title: Applied Analysis
author: John K. Hunter, et al
description: This book provides an introduction to those parts of analysis that are most useful in applications for graduate students. The material is selected for use in applied problems, and is presented clearly and simply but without sacrificing mathematical rigor.

title: Calculus: Theory and Applications
author: Kenneth Kuttler
description: This is a book on single variable calculus including most of the important applications of calculus. It also includes proofs of all theorems presented, either in the text itself, or in an appendix. It also contains an introduction to vectors and vector products.

title: Advanced Calculus
author: Lynn H. Loomis, et al
description: Problem solving and mathematical modeling are introduced early and reinforced throughout, providing students with a solid foundation in the principles of mathematical thinking.

title: Active Calculus
author: Matt Boelkins
description: Rather than detailed explanations and worked out examples, this book uses activities intended to be done by the students in order to present the standard concepts and computational techniques of calculus.

title: Vector Calculus
author: Michael Corral
description: This is a text on elementary multivariable calculus, designed for students who have completed courses in single-variable calculus. Concepts are amply illustrated with figures, worked examples, and physical applications.

title: Calculus
author: WikiBooks
description: This wikibook aims to be a high quality calculus textbook through which users can master the discipline. Standard topics such as limits, differentiation and integration are covered, as well as several others.

title: Introduction to Mathematical Analysis
author: Beatriz Lafferriere, et al
description: The goal of this book is to provide students with a strong foundation in mathematical analysis. Such a foundation is crucial for future study of deeper topics of analysis. It will be reinforced through rigorous proofs.

title: Complex Variables: Second Edition
author: Robert B. Ash, et al
description: This text on complex variables is geared toward who have taken an introductory course in real analysis. Offering a concise treatment that provides careful and complete explanations as well as numerous problems and solutions.

title: Theory of the Integral
author: Brian S. Thomson
description: This text is intended as a treatise for a rigorous course introducing the elements of integration theory on the real line. All of the important features of the Riemann integral, the Lebesgue integral, and the Henstock-Kurzweil integral are covered.

title: Complex Integration and Cauchy's Theorem
author: G.N. Watson
description: This brief monograph by one of the great mathematicians offers a single-volume compilation of propositions employed in proofs of Cauchy's theorem, provides a brief account of the various applications of the theorem to the evaluation of definite integrals.

title: Basic Real Analysis
author: Anthony W. Knapp
description: This is a comprehensive treatment with a global view of the Real Analysis, emphasizing the connections between real analysis and other branches of mathematics. Included throughout are many examples and hundreds of problems.

title: A Primer of Real Analysis
author: Dan Sloughter
description: This is a short introduction to the fundamentals of real analysis, written the text assuming the reader has the level of mathematical maturity of one who has completed the standard sequence of calculus courses.

title: Introduction to Real Analysis
author: William F. Trench
description: Using an extremely clear and informal approach, this book introduces readers to a rigorous understanding of mathematical analysis and presents challenging math concepts as clearly as possible.

title: Interactive Real Analysis
author: Bert G. Wachsmuth
description: An interactive textbook for Real Analysis or Advanced Calculus in one real variable. It deals with sets, sequences, series, continuity, differentiability, integrability (Riemann and Lebesgue), topology, power series, and more.

title: Integrate Your Brain: How To Do Calculus In Your Head
author: Unknown
description: This book teaches how talented mathematicians utilize their normal, human mental ability to tackle calculus. You are gently trained in the fundamental skills, and shown step by step how to put them into action yourself.

title: Mathematical Analysis I
author: Elias Zakon
description: This book carefully leads the student through the basic topics of real analysis. Topics include metric spaces, open and closed sets, convergent sequences, function limits and continuity, compact sets, sequences and series of functions, power series, etc.

title: Mathematical Analysis II
author: Elias Zakon
description: It is for any second course in real analysis or mathematical analysis, covering Banach spaces, measure theory (with a complete discussion of outer measures, Lebesgue measure, Lebesgue-Stieltjes measures, and differentiation of set functions), etc.

title: Elementary Calculus: An Infinitesimal Approach
author: H. Jerome Keisler
description: This first-year calculus book is centered around the use of infinitesimals. It contains all the ordinary calculus topics, including the basic concepts of the derivative, continuity, and the integral, plus traditional limit concepts and approximation problems.

title: Foundations of Infinitesimal Calculus
author: H. Jerome Keisler
description: This monograph is a companion to the Author's textbook. It can be used as a quick introduction to the infinitesimal approach to calculus for mathematicians, as background material for instructors, or as a text for an undergraduate seminar.

title: Mathematical Background: Foundations of Infinitesimal
author: Unknown
description: We wrote this book of foundations in part to provide a convenient reference for a student who might like to see the "theorem - proof" approach to calculus. It also shows how the pathologies arise in the traditional approach.

title: Nonstandard Analysish
author: Jaap Ponstein, et al.
description: This book is concerned with an attempt to introduce the infinitesimals and the other 'nonstandard' numbers in a naive, simpleminded way. Nevertheless, the resulting theory is hoped to be mathematically sound, and to be complete within obvious limits.

title: Special Functions: Fractional Calculus and the Pathway for Entropy
author: Unknown
description: This book deals with the connection between entropy, probability, and fractional dynamics as they appeared, for example, in solar neutrino astrophysics. This analysis revealed a non-Gaussian signal with harmonic content.

title: Linear Mathematics In Infinite Dimensions
author: Ulrich H. Gerlach
description: Focus on the mathematical framework that underlies linear systems arising in physics, engineering and applied mathematics - from the theory of linear transformation on finite dimensional vector space to the infinite dimensional vector spaces.

title: First Course in the Theory of Equations
author: Leonard Dickson
description: The theory of equations is not only a necessity in the subsequent mathematical courses and their applications, but furnishes an illuminating sequel to geometry, algebra and analytic geometry. A useful supplement to differential calculus.

title: Analysis and Linear Algebra for Finance
author: Patrick Roger
description: This book present the elements of analysis and linear algebra used in financial models and in microeconomics. It provides a broad overview of the mathematics of financial models. Functions of one and several variables and matrices are developed.

title: Mastering Linux: From Zero to Advanced Expertise
author: Ayman Alheraki
description: A single unifying goal: to transform the reader from a casual user into a fully competent expert capable of understanding, configuring, administering, programming, and extending modern Linux systems—with precision and confidence.

title: Linux Fundamentals
author: Paul Cobbaut
description: This book provides a soft, accessible, and practical introduction to Linux environments and command line basics, from a basic approach to Linux to a more advanced server-oriented look at using Linux.

title: Linux for Beginners
author: Jason Cannon
description: This book discusses the ins and outs of Linux in a beginner friendly style to make your learning process frustration free, includes Command Line, Programming and Operating System, as the book does not assume you know anything about Linux.

title: Just Enough Linux
author: Malcolm Maclean
description: This book aims at getting you comfortable with some of the commands used in Linux. If you've toyed with Linux and never really caught on to what's happening or have used a graphical interface without really touching the command line this book is for you.

title: Linux with Operating System Concepts
author: Richard Fox
description: This book merges conceptual operating system (OS) and Unix/Linux topics into one cohesive textbook for undergraduate students, covers Linux from both the user and system administrator positions.

author: Unknown

title: Embedded Linux System Development: Practical Labs
author: Bootlin
description: Get your hands on an embedded board based on an ARM processor, and apply what you learned to implement real-time requirements so that you can quickly turn your ideas into a working prototype!

title: Embedded Linux
author: Karim Yaghmour
description: There's a great deal of excitement surrounding the use of Linux in embedded systems - but not a lot of practical information. This book offers an in-depth, hard-core guide to putting together embedded systems based on Linux.

title: Introduction to Embedded Linux: Lab Instructions
author: TTO
description: A real-world hands-on guide to building efficient, high-value, embedded systems with Linux. You'll learn how to build a modern, efficient embedded Linux development environment, and then utilize it as productively as possible.

title: Embedded Linux System Design and Development
author: Unknown
description: This book contains a full embedded Linux system development roadmap for systems architects and software programmers, delivers practical solutions for writing, debugging, and profiling applications and drivers in embedded Linux.

title: Building Embedded Linux Systems
author: Karim Yaghmour
description: This book is the hard-core guide to putting together an embedded system based on the Linux kernel, gives you the basics of building embedded Linux systems, along with the configuration, setup, and use open source and free software packages.

title: Ten Steps to Linux Survival: Navigating the Bash Jungle
author: Unknown
description: Provides proven steps and strategies on learning what Linux is and how to use it. It contains information on the Linux Operating System, especially for beginners, leads you through some diagnostic and recovery tasks so you can quickly get your site back up.

title: LINUX: Rute User's Tutorial and Exposition
author: Paul Sheer
description: This book is the best book on the market in terms of flattening that learning curve of Linux. It tries to inculcate its readers into the Linux way of thinking. No matter what kind of Linux systems you're using, it presents the techniques you need to succeed.

title: Linux Inside
author: 0xAX
description: This is a book about the linux kernel and its insides. The goal to share modest knowledge about the insides of the linux kernel and help people who are interested in linux kernel insides, and other low-level subject matter.

title: Knowing Knoppix: The Beginner's Guide To Linux
author: Phil Jones, et al
description: Knoppix is an astoundingly clever product. It runs Linux completely from CD. It bypasses all the software already installed on your PC or laptop. This book is a beginner-friendly book designed to help with these situations: You can't start Windows!

title: Linux From Scratch
author: Gerard Beekmans, et al
description: It's a set of books that provides you with step-by-step instructions for building your own customized Linux system entirely from source, the ultimate hands-on Linux user guide, whether you're a true beginner or a more advanced user navigating recent changes.

title: The Linux Command Line: A Complete Introduction
author: W. E. Shotts
description: This book takes you from your very first terminal keystrokes to writing full programs in Bash, the most popular Linux shell. Along the way you'll learn the timeless skills handed down by generations of gray-bearded, mouse-shunning gurus.

title: Conquering the Command Line: Unix and Linux for Developers
author: Unknown
description: You will find not only the most useful command line tools for Unix and Linux based systems you need to know, but also the most helpful options and flags for those tools. It makes you instantly more productive in your daily development life.

title: Step-by-Step Linux Guide

description: This ebook describes the system administration aspects of using Linux and is intended for people who know nothing about system administration. This Linux ebook doesn't tell you how to install Linux since it is very straight forward but it gives you real world mail, DNS, proxy, web, messaging etc server installations and configurations.

title: O'Reilly® Linux Kernel in a Nutshell
author: Greg Kroah-Hartman
description: Written by a leading developer and maintainer of the Linux kernel,this bookl is a comprehensive overview of kernel configuration and building, a critical task for Linux users and administrators.

title: Linux Client Migration Cookbook: Migrating to Desktop Linux

title: Linux 101 Hacks

description: There are total of 101 hacks in this book that will help you build a strong foundation in Linux. All the hacks are explained with appropriate Linux command examples that are easy to follow.

author: Unknown

title: Into the Core: A look at Tiny Core Linux
author: Lauri Kasanen, et al

author: Neil Smyth
description: This book is designed to provide detailed information on the installation, use and administration of the Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) distribution. For beginners, the book covers topics for both beginners and experienced users.

title: The SELinux Notebook, 4th Edition
author: Richard Haines
description: If you want an effective means of securing your Linux system (and who doesn't?), this book provides the means. This best-known and most respected security-related extension to Linux embodies the key advances of the security field.

title: Learning Old School Linux
author: Ed Hartnett
description: Linux has long been regarded by engineers as the superior operating system. If you are looking for a simple, basic overview of everything Linux-related, look no further than this compilation of articles written for ComputorEdge magazine from 2003-2010.

title: Bodhi Linux 3 for Beginners
author: Roger Carter
description: Based on the popular Ubuntu operating system, Bodhi Linux 3 incorporates the latest version of the elegant Enlightenment desktop manager. This book explains in easy steps how to install Bodhi Linux on your computer, how to customize and use it, etc.

title: Step-by-Step Guide to Bodhi Linux
author: Roger Carter
description: This book is suitable for anyone migrating to Linux from Windows, and explains in easy steps how to install Bodhi Linux on your computer, how to customize and use it, and how to install a range of recommended applications.

title: Linux Mint Essentials
author: Jay LaCroix
description: This book is an all-inclusive guide to Linux Mint, and will teach you everything you need to know in order to use a Linux Mint system. It guide walks the reader through installing and maintaining Linux Mint on a personal computer.

title: Linux Succinctly
author: Jason Cannon
description: This book will teach you the basics of interacting with Linux, such as viewing and editing files and directories through the command line, and how to modify permissions. More advanced topics covered include I/O streams, sorting and comparing files and directories, and installing additional software.

title: Getting Started with Ubuntu
author: The Ubuntu Manual Team
description: This free book is a complete beginners manual for Ubuntu, featuring comprehensive guides, How Tos and information on anything you need to know after first installing Ubuntu.

title: Linux Quick Fix Notebook
author: Peter Harrison
description: This books includes many of the most commonly encountered errors with explanations of their causes and how to fix them. The book's format is aimed at sys admins who often have to do advanced tasks in which the underlying theory is understood,

title: Self-Service Linux
author: Mastering the Art of Problem Determination
description: A book that advanced Linux professionals running their own Linux systems will be able to use to troubleshoot, an essential part of every company's Linux adoption plan to keep the total cost of ownership (TCO)down and improve the ROI of their Linux strategy.

title: Linux Patch Management: Keeping Linux Systems Up To Date
author: Unknown
description: This book is the first start-to-finish guide to patching Linux systems in production environments. It presents patching solutions for Red Hat, Fedora, SUSE, Debian, and other distributions, covers both distribution-specific tools and widely used tools.

title: User Mode Linux
author: Jeff Dike
description: This book covers everything from getting started through running enterprise-class User Mode Linux servers. You'll find authoritative advice on bootup, compilation, administration, specialized configurations, and much more.

title: The Daemon, the Gnu, and the Penguin
author: Peter H. Salus
description: In addition to covering a history of free and open source, This book explores how free and open software is changing the world. The author interviewed well over a hundred key figures to document the history and background of free and open source software.

title: Understanding the Linux Virtual Memory Manager
author: Mel Gorman
description: This book is unique in that not only does it describe the Linux Memory Manager itself in unprecedented detail, it also includes the theoretical foundations for both developers and students but has been omitted from recent Linux kernel related material.

title: The Linux Development Platform
author: Rafeeq Ur Rehman, et al
description: This book describes how to build a development environment based upon Linux systems. It provides a one-stop reference on all the tools used by the Open Source community for development purposes.

author: Unknown

author: Bob Smith, et al
description: This book shows how to build better appliances - appliances with more types of interfaces, more dynamic interfaces, and better debugged interfaces. You'll learn how to build backend daemons, handle asynchronous events, and connect various user interfaces.

title: Linux 101 Examination Modular Training Notes
author: Andrew McGill

title: Linux 102 Examination Modular Training Notes
author: Andrew McGill

title: Linux Professional Institute Certification (LPIC) Examination Guide
author: Unknown
description: This book is a collection of self-study articles and tutorials to help you learn Linux fundamentals and prepare for system administrator certification.

title: Kali Linux Wireless Penetration Testing Beginner's Guide
author: Unknown
description: This book presents wireless pentesting from the ground up, introducing all elements of penetration testing with each new technology. Learn various wireless testing methodologies by example, from the basics of wireless routing to detailed coverage.

title: Linux Network Administrator's Guide, 3rd Ed.
author: Tony Bautts
description: Dispense all the practical advice you need to join a network. Along with some hardware considerations, look at all of the essential networking software that comes with the operating system--including (TCP/IP, wireless networking, firewalling), etc.

title: O'Reilly® Ubuntu Hacks: Tips/Tools for Exploring, Using Linux
author: Unknown
description: This is your one-stop source for all of the community knowledge you need to get the most out of Ubuntu: a collection of 100 tips and tools to help new and experienced Linux users install, configure, and customize Ubuntu.

description: This book is designed to provide detailed information on the use and administration of the CentOS 6 Linux distribution.

title: Programming Linux Games

description: This book is a complete guide to developing Linux games, written by the Linux gaming experts. It discusses important multimedia toolkits and teaches the basics of Linux game programming.

author: SSC
description: This book introduces Linux users to the desktop capabilities of Linux and the K Desktop Environment (KDE) graphical user interface, a powerful Open Source graphical desktop environment for UNIX workstations.

description: This book takes the reader step by step through the process of installing and setting up a Debian system, and provides a thorough but gentle introduction to the basics of using Debian GNU/Linux.

title: O'Reilly® Linux Device Drivers, 3rd Edition
author: Jonathan Corbet
description: The 3rd edition of Linux Device Drivers is better than ever. The book covers all the significant changes to Version 2.6 of the Linux kernel, which simplifies many activities, and contains subtle new features.

title: O'Reilly® Linux Device Drivers, 2nd Edition
author: Alessandro Rubini, et al
description: This book is for anyone who wants to support computer peripherals under the Linux operating system or who wants to develop new hardware and run it under Linux.

author: Alan Hicks, et al
description: This Book is designed to get you started with Slackware Linux operating system. It`s not meant to cover every single aspect of the distribution, but rather to show what it is capable of and give you a basic working knowledge of the system.

title: Ubuntu 10.x Essentials
author: Neil Smyth
description: The purpose of this book is to provide an overview of the essential knowledge required to use and maintain an Ubuntu system.

title: CentOS Essentials
author: Neil Smyth
description: This is a book designed to provide detailed information on the use and administration of the CentOS Linux distribution. It's for both beginners and experienced user, covers together with all the important topics.

description: This book demystifies the Linux audio system set-up, describes basic and advanced use of the system, and profiles the broad range of sound and music applications and development software available for Linux.

title: O'Reilly® Test Driving Linux: From Windows to Linux in 60 Seconds
author: Unknown
description: This book is a detailed step-by-step guide to the Linux operating system and several popular open source programs. It provides both home and business users with a hassle-free way to investigate this operating system before they purchase and install a complete Linux distribution.
